### How this work is cited

Passages inside Peau noire, masques blancs are identified by chapter, or the conclusion. The chapter the archive cites most is the conclusion. The Markmann translation, which is the one in general English circulation, is known to compress and occasionally omit passages, so a locator without a translator leaves the wording's provenance open — the archive records the translator where it can.

### The work in Frantz Fanon’s thought

Frantz Fanon (1925–1961) was a Martinican psychiatrist and anti-colonial theorist who practiced in Algeria and joined the FLN. Black Skin, White Masks analyzes the psychic effects of antiblack racism; The Wretched of the Earth theorizes decolonization, violence, and national culture. [More on Frantz Fanon](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/frantz-fanon) .
